answer: In Discord's legacy search fleet, a shard could be healthy yet incomplete because the loss happened upstream of Elasticsearch. Realtime indexing fed the search index asynchronously through a Redis-backed queue; when search-node failures built a backlog, Redis became CPU-saturated and began dropping messages. Those messages never entered the index pipeline, so they were absent from the index rather than temporarily unavailable, and querying a healthy shard later could not recover them. "Healthy" describes cluster/shard state, not whether every produced message was successfully indexed. Fan-out bulk ingestion amplified the pressure: a 50-message batch could target 50 nodes, and one unavailable node failed the whole batch and forced retries. Discord later replaced Redis with a backlog-retaining PubSub queue and grouped bulk writes by destination, but the source leaves queue redelivery/idempotency, prolonged-outage retention, and consistent index checkpoints unvalidated, and does not establish a reliable source store for regenerating every lost item. Completeness therefore requires ingest-offset/record reconciliation, not only green shard health.
